title: La Paz coalition march against the Health Emergency Law
location: From Adepcoca in Villa Fátima toward Plaza Murillo, La Paz
organizer: Coca growers, medical workers and urban teachers; specific convenor not established
threshold_50_evidence: The opened reports identify participating sectors but provide no simultaneous attendance count; the >=50 threshold is unverified.

start_date.summary: ERBOL and ANF describe a La Paz march on 22 February; ANF places the national doctors’ strike at its fourth day.

location.summary: March route ran from Adepcoca in Villa Fátima toward Plaza Murillo.

organizer.summary: Coca growers, medical workers and urban teachers joined; a convening body is not named.

demands.summary: The march included a demand to repeal the Health Emergency Law; ERBOL also lists private-property and unionization demands.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Neither opened article counts simultaneous marchers.

protester_violence.summary: ERBOL reports that marchers threw stones, firecrackers and other objects at the police cordon; this single report is not independently corroborated.

state_response.crowd_dispersal.summary: ERBOL reports police tear gas and clearing the route.

notes: A distinct 22 February street march during the post-promulgation law campaign. Later dated assemblies are not merged with it. One source reports objects used against police; the conduct is attributed to that report, not independently verified.
open_questions: Verify simultaneous crowd size, event-specific organization and source attribution for reported protester violence.

title: La Paz health-law coalition mobilization, second day
organizer: Doctors, coca growers and teachers; specific convenor not established
threshold_50_evidence: ANF describes a second day of mobilization but gives no count for the cocalero/medical/teacher gathering; the >=50 threshold is unverified.

start_date.summary: ANF dates the second day of La Paz mobilization to 23 February.

location.summary: The march and police dispersal are located in central La Paz.

organizer.summary: Doctors, coca growers and teachers participated; the exact convenor is not identified.

demands.summary: The health-sector group demanded repeal of the Health Emergency Law.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: No simultaneous participant count is given.

state_response.crowd_dispersal.summary: ANF reports police chemical agents used to disperse the mobilization.

protester_violence.summary: ANF relays a Unitel-attributed report of two injured police officers, including a firecracker injury; attribution to this coalition is not established.

notes: A separately dated street action on the second day of mobilization. ANF also describes a distinct Normal Simón Bolívar applicants’ protest that day; the two gatherings are not pooled. The officer-injury report is attributed to Unitel and is not treated as independent corroboration or assigned to one gathering.
open_questions: Verify crowd size and which gathering experienced the reported police dispersal and injuries.

title: Normal Simón Bolívar applicants protest admissions process
location: Central La Paz, near the Normal Simón Bolívar admissions dispute
organizer: Applicants to the Normal Simón Bolívar teacher-training institute
threshold_50_evidence: ANF reports a separate applicants’ protest but supplies no simultaneous participant estimate; the >=50 threshold is unverified.

start_date.summary: ANF reports the applicants’ action on 23 February.

location.summary: The report places the action among the central La Paz mobilizations and identifies Normal Simón Bolívar applicants.

organizer.summary: Applicants to Normal Simón Bolívar are identified; no organization is named.

demands.summary: Applicants sought admission after alleged irregularities in the entrance examination.

notes: ANF distinguishes this admissions dispute from the health-law and coca-grower action. Whether the institution’s admissions decision constitutes the relevant domestic state-policy target requires review; no state response is safely assigned to this gathering.
open_questions: Verify simultaneous crowd size, responsible state decision-maker and whether the admissions grievance fits the domestic-policy target rule.

title: Departmental-capital health-sector marches against Law 1359
location: Cochabamba downtown, Santa Cruz main plaza and Oruro; other capitals are not individually specified
organizer: Public and private health workers; CONASA called the ten-day national strike
participants_original: No city-specific crowd count reported; Oruro’s 95% figure is sector strike adherence, not assembly turnout.
threshold_50_evidence: Los Tiempos reports marches in several capitals but gives no simultaneous attendance count by site; counts cannot be pooled across cities, so the >=50 threshold is unverified at each.

start_date.summary: Los Tiempos, published 25 February, dates these marches to 24 February.

location.summary: The report names central Cochabamba, a white-coat march to Santa Cruz’s main plaza and an Oruro march.

organizer.summary: Public and private health workers marched during the ten-day strike called by CONASA.

demands.summary: Participants sought repeal of the Health Emergency Law and requested dialogue.

participants_original.summary: The article reports 95% strike adherence in Oruro, which is not crowd size.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: No assembly count by city; workforce adherence cannot substitute for attendance.

notes: This is a same-day, multi-location candidate only for review. Do not add attendance across departmental capitals or treat a strike-adherence percentage as a crowd estimate.
open_questions: Find city-specific simultaneous crowd estimates and decide whether the nationally called marches represent one coordinated event or separate local events.

title: Health workers’ “blockade of the thousand corners”
location: Several Bolivian cities; the article does not list all cities or individual intersections
organizer: Public and private health-sector workers during the CONASA-called strike
threshold_50_evidence: Los Tiempos says the action occurred in several cities but gives no number of people at any intersection; the >=50 threshold cannot be inferred from the label or number of corners.

start_date.summary: Los Tiempos says the blockade of the thousand corners took place the day before its 26 February publication.

location.summary: The article reports several cities without enumerating the sites.

organizer.summary: The article attributes the action to the health sector participating in the ten-day strike.

demands.summary: The strike and street actions sought repeal or modification of the Health Emergency Law.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: No number of people at a gathering is reported.

notes: The 26 February report documents this as an executed action on 25 February, while the separate announced 1 March roadblocks or hunger strike remain future plans. The event’s locations and physical duration are not fully specified.
open_questions: Identify actual sites and simultaneous turnout, and determine whether these were separate gatherings or a synchronized campaign action.

title: La Paz doctors march to the Health Ministry
location: La Paz, march to the Ministry of Health
organizer: Doctors and health-sector workers; local convening organization not identified
participants_original: Los Tiempos describes “some hundreds” of doctors marching in La Paz; exact number and range are not stated.
threshold_50_evidence: “Some hundreds” of doctors is a qualitative estimate above the 50-person threshold. No exact attendance total is reported.

start_date.summary: Los Tiempos, published 27 February, reports the La Paz march took place the prior day, 26 February.

location.summary: The article says doctors marched to the Ministry of Health in La Paz.

organizer.summary: The march involved doctors within the public/private health-sector strike; a local organizing body is not specified.

demands.summary: The health sector demanded repeal of the Health Emergency Law.

participants_original.summary: Los Tiempos describes “some hundreds” of doctors in La Paz.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: The qualitative phrase “some hundreds” supports >=50 but provides no exact count or defensible numeric interval.

notes: This is a distinct physical La Paz march with the only body-verified crowd estimate meeting the threshold. The Government’s openness to dialogue about regulation is not a verified concession or an event-specific response.
open_questions: Coordinator to review the qualitative attendance wording, official-baseline fit and exact event/campaign boundary.

title: Cochabamba health-sector march against Law 1359
organizer: Public and private health-sector workers; local convening organization not identified
threshold_50_evidence: Los Tiempos reports a march but no simultaneous participant count; the >=50 threshold is unverified.

start_date.summary: Los Tiempos, published 27 February, reports a Cochabamba march the prior day, 26 February.

location.summary: The report describes health workers marching through central Cochabamba.

organizer.summary: Public and private health workers participated; a local convening body is not specified.

demands.summary: The health sector demanded repeal of the Health Emergency Law.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: No count is reported for Cochabamba; La Paz’s estimate is not transferred to this separate gathering.

notes: Keep this Cochabamba gathering separate from the La Paz march. The La Paz estimate does not establish the threshold at this site.
open_questions: Verify attendance at Cochabamba and other unspecified cities reported on 26 February.

title: Anapo soy-producer road blockades over the price band
location: Roads in Santa Cruz department, including Pailón and the Bridge of Friendship; active sites varied
participants_original: Not reported; articles identify blockade locations and producers but not simultaneous persons.
threshold_50_evidence: No source gives a simultaneous participant count at any blockade point; vehicles, roads and number of sites cannot establish >=50 people.

start_date.summary: Los Tiempos reports the blockades began on 22 February; Red Uno independently says they began Monday 22 February.

location.summary: Pailón was a reported initial point. By 26 February, several points had been lifted and the Bridge of Friendship remained blocked.

organizer.summary: Anapo and soy producers are identified as organizers/participants.

demands.summary: The central demand was removal or revision of the government price band for soy derivatives; the Unitel-origin republication also mentions export and biotechnology demands.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: No simultaneous crowd count appears in these opened accounts.

state_response.accommodation.summary: Red Uno reports repeated talks/intermissions with national authorities and negotiations scheduled to resume while the Bridge of Friendship remained blocked; this is contact, not a verified concession.

notes: Anapo’s road action is separate from the health-law campaign. Several Santa Cruz sites were partially reopened by 26 February, but the Bridge of Friendship remained blocked. A 25 February Unitel-origin report republished by eju.tv says organizers intended to lift that bridge blockade that night; it does not verify closure. The physical end date remains unknown.
open_questions: Verify a qualifying simultaneous crowd at a site, site-by-site coordination, and any dated physical end after the 26 February report.
